settings.title: Web tracking
settings.lead: Add one line to your website and see what visitors do before they ever sign in.

snippet.title: Tracking snippet
snippet.description: Paste this snippet into the head section of your website, on every page. The script has no dependencies and weighs {size}.
snippet.key_hint: The public key is visible in your page source and that is fine. It can only write events and cannot read anything from the project.
snippet.consent_note: Without consent the script writes and stores nothing. Pass consent by calling Mlain.consent once the visitor grants it.

domains.title: Tracking domains
domains.description: The script only runs on the domains listed here. Without at least one domain, web tracking will not start.
domains.unverified: Not verified yet. Verification happens automatically on the first successful script run.
domains.empty: There is no domain here yet, so tracking will not start anywhere.
domains.internal: Internal address. Works only from this computer or from your network.
domains.limit: You can have at most {limit} tracking domains.

status.waiting: No event has arrived from your website yet.
status.waiting_hint: After you add the snippet, the first event shows up within seconds. Check that your website domain is in the list above.
status.receiving: In the last 30 days: {events, plural, =0 {no events} one {# event} other {# events}} from {visitors, plural, =0 {no visitors} one {# visitor} other {# visitors}}.

reach.title: The tracking domain is not reachable from the internet
reach.loopback: The tracking domain is {host}, which is this computer's own address. Nobody can reach it from another website or from an inbox.
reach.private: The tracking domain is {host}, which is only reachable from your network. Nobody can reach it from another website or from an inbox.
reach.invalid: The tracking domain {host} is not a valid address.
reach.consequence: Email opens will therefore not be recorded at all: Gmail and others fetch the image through their own servers and those cannot reach this address. Web events only arrive from a browser on this computer.
reach.fix: When you move to production, point TRACKING_DOMAIN at a public domain, for example t.yourdomain.com.

identify.title: Identifying a signed-in visitor
identify.description: When a visitor on your site is known to you, tell tracking by calling Mlain.identify. From that moment events are tied to a specific contact, including the ones collected anonymously before.
identify.unsigned_hint: You pass only your own customer identifier and traits without personal data. The server finds an existing contact by that identifier. It never creates a new one and never changes the email.
identify.signed_hint: Only a signed call may pass an email or phone and create a new contact. Without a signature the server rejects such a call, because anyone can read the code in the browser and could otherwise forge someone else's address.
identify.key_note: The key is the digest of the secret, not the secret itself: the server never stores the private key in readable form, only its SHA-256 digest. The secret is the fourth and last part of the key, the one after the third underscore. It contains underscores itself, so never split it on the last one. The jcs canonicalization is the JSON Canonicalization Scheme per RFC 8785, meaning sorted keys, no whitespace between tokens and accented characters written as they are.
identify.ascii_note: The examples sort keys with a plain sort, which matches RFC 8785 for ordinary names made of letters and digits. If you use trait names with accented characters, reach for a ready RFC 8785 library, otherwise the ordering may diverge.
identify.rejected_note: When the signature does not match, the event is stored in tracking but nothing is applied to the contact. Check that you sign the same data you send and that a single newline separates the identifier from the traits.
